mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase the present value of future cash flows. This relationship holds continuously without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when FEDFUNDS is in the lowest quartile compared to the highest quartile (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit expectations, which cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 109.0) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE above 4.0) signals an imminent economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as investors price in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 109.0 and UNRATE > 4.0 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle (FEDFUNDS below 3.0%), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 days as lower rates stimulate economic activity and equity valuations. This mechanism is active only during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units signals reduced consumer confidence and lower residential investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as the housing sector is a key component of GDP.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1200.0 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) is associated with stronger corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as the manufacturing sector expands.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when INDPRO is in the highest quartile compared to the lowest quartile (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals persistent inflation that may lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate higher interest rates and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3.5 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A stronger labor market, indicated by higher employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 thousand persons, is associated with increased consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when PAYEMS is above 150,000 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
